title: A universally exact sequence with finitely presented quotient splits
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A,B,C$ be $R$-modules, and let $i:A\to B$ and $p:B\to C$ be $R$-linear maps with $i$ injective, $p$ surjective and $\ker p=i(A)$. Suppose $C$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Suppose also that for every $R$-module $Q$ the sequence $0\to A\otimes_RQ\xrightarrow{i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q}B\otimes_RQ\xrightarrow{p\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q}C\otimes_RQ\to0$ is exact, meaning that its first map is injective, its last map is surjective and the image of its first map is the kernel of its last map [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then there exists an $R$-linear map $r:B\to A$ satisfying $r\circ i=\mathrm{id}_A$. No finite-generation or flatness assumption on $A$ or $B$ is made.
